To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel series of poly(PEGA) 30-block-poly(L-Lys)25-block-poly(L-His)n (n = 50, 100) copolymer vesicles were fabricated and characterized for tumoral pH-triggered controlled release of doxorubicin.
a series of novel pH-responsive poly(ethylene glycols) methyl ether acylate-block-poly(L-hisidine) [p (PEGA) 30-b-p(L-His)n] hybrid vesicles were synthesized for intracellular delivery.
a series of pH-sensitive hybrid vesicles were designed and synthesized, and their potential for controlled and targeted intracellular release of Dox was investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of pH-responsive hybrid vesicle system for the intracellular delivery of anticancer drugs.

the design, synthesis, characterization, and evaluation of a series of pH-responsive hybrid vesicle systems based on poly(ethylene glycols) methyl ether acylate-block-poly(L-Lysine)-block-p-poly(L-His) for intracellular delivery.

a novel approach for the preparation and characterization of pH-triggered hybrid vesicles based on a triblock copolymethacrylate-block-copolypeptide for the intracellular delivery of anticancer drug Dox.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work demonstrates the potential of these hybrid vesicle systems for tumor-targeted drug delivery.
the pH-responsive vesicle-based drug delivery system is a promising candidate for intracellular delivery and tumor-targeted chemotherapy.
the p(PEGA)-p(Lys)-p(His) triblock copolymer-based hybrid vesicles are a promising pH-responsive drug delivery system for the intracellular delivery of hydrophilic drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pH-responsive vesicles can be used for the controlled release of anticancer agents, and the vesicles can be further functionalized for the targeted delivery of drugs.

we have developed a series of pH-responsive vesicles for intracellular delivery and release of Dox and the vesicles were found to be nontoxic to normal cells and showed dose-dependent cytotoxic effect on CT26 cells in vitro.
we have designed a novel poly(L-lysine) and poly(L-histidine)-containing hybrid vesicles, which could be used as a drug delivery vehicle for the intracellular release of Dox at tumor sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pH-triggered release of Dox can be achieved by a simple and straightforward method.
we have developed pH-responsive hybrid vesicle for tumor-targeted drug delivery.

pH-triggered release of Dox from vesicular carriers could be a promising approach for cancer therapeutics and that these hybrid vesicles could be used as a platform for tumor-specific controlled release of anticancer drugs.
